CloudTrail

The topic is now confirmed by the project owner, so the technical article is populated. The canonical ledger status is not promoted until the original published artifact is recovered.

AWS CloudTrail records account activity so operators can answer who or what called an AWS API, when it happened, from where and against which resources.

Architecture / mental model

Console / CLI / SDK / AWS service action → CloudTrail event → Event History / trail / CloudTrail Lake → audit & detection

How it works

CloudTrail records AWS account activity as events, including management actions from the Management Console, CLI, SDKs and AWS services. Event records carry identity, event time, service/action and request context useful for audit and incident response.

Event History automatically provides recent management-event history for an AWS account/Region. For ongoing retention and broader event selection, a trail or CloudTrail Lake event data store is configured.

CloudTrail and CloudWatch are complementary. CloudTrail is primarily about activity/audit history; CloudWatch is primarily about operational telemetry such as metrics, logs, alarms and dashboards. CloudTrail events can also be delivered into CloudWatch Logs for detection workflows.

Hands-on reference

aws cloudtrail lookup-events --max-results 20
aws cloudtrail describe-trails
aws cloudtrail get-trail-status --name TRAIL_NAME

Verification

Perform a harmless API action, then locate the corresponding CloudTrail event and identify the principal, source, action and resource context. Confirm trail delivery if long-term logging is configured.

Field note / gotcha

Seeing recent management events in Event History does not mean you have configured long-term logging for every event type you care about. Data events and other event classes require deliberate selection/configuration.

Security considerations

Use multi-Region/organization logging where appropriate, protect log destinations from tampering, restrict trail changes and build alerts for high-risk administrative actions.

What I learned

When an AWS resource changes unexpectedly, CloudTrail is where 'somebody changed it' becomes a concrete identity, API call and timestamp.
